Level B

Specialisation: Brute & Scout

Create subclasses with unique abilities

What You'll Learn

1 Create a subclass that inherits from a parent class
2 Override attributes after calling the parent constructor (optional method override)
3 Understand polymorphism — same method, different results

Key Terms

Term Definition
Inheritance A class deriving from another class, gaining its attributes and methods
Subclass A class that inherits from another (also called child class)
Parent Class The class being inherited from (also called superclass)
Override Replacing or specialising inherited behaviour or values in the subclass
Polymorphism Same method name produces different behaviour based on object type

Class Design (UML)

△ Inherits from (IS-A)
[override] Extends parent behaviour

Brute and Scout also implement describe_specialty() to demonstrate method overriding.

OOP Spotlight: Overriding vs Tweaking Data

Attribute override: In this level, Brute and Scout change values like health and accuracy after calling super(). Same methods, different data.

Method override: You can also change behaviour by overriding a method. This is optional and not required by the validator.

Optional extension: Override get_status() in Brute or Scout to include the class name (e.g., "Brute Alex: 120/120 HP"). Keep the same method name and return type.

This makes polymorphism visible: the engine calls the same method, but each class can respond differently.

Structure Guide

Click each section to expand. You'll create TWO new classes in a new file.

1 Import the Parent Class
IMPORT Player FROM student.player
You need access to Player so your new classes can inherit from it.
2 Create the Brute Class
CLASS Brute INHERITS FROM Player:
The Tank Archetype: Create a constructor that:
  • Calls the parent constructor first (pass the name)
  • Then overrides: health = 120, max_health = 120
  • armour = 3
  • accuracy = 70
Hint: Use super() to call the parent constructor, then set the attributes you want to change.
3 Create the Scout Class
CLASS Scout INHERITS FROM Player:
The Precision Archetype: Create a constructor that:
  • Calls the parent constructor first (pass the name)
  • Then overrides: health = 80, max_health = 80
  • armour = 1
  • accuracy = 95
Hint: Same pattern as Brute — call parent first, then customise.
4 Add describe_specialty()
METHOD describe_specialty() → string:
Return a short description of what makes the class unique.
  • Brute: high health and armour
  • Scout: high accuracy and mobility
This shows method overriding: same method name, different output.
5 How Inheritance Works
Both Brute and Scout inherit from Player, meaning they get all Player methods (get_status, take_damage, heal) for free.

By calling the parent constructor and then overriding specific attributes, each class becomes a specialised version of Player with its own stats.

By overriding describe_specialty(), each class can also change behaviour while keeping the same method name.

brute = Brute("Tank")
scout = Scout("Ghost")

Both work with any code that expects a Player — that's the power of inheritance.

Your Mission

Create Player Specialisations

The station's security system offers you a choice: register as a Brute (tough but imprecise) or a Scout (fragile but accurate).

Create student/player_types.py with both classes. Each must inherit from Player and customise their stats in the constructor.
